scenes.title: Cloud Monitoring & Logging
scenes.narration: Monitoring and logging services like CloudWatch collect metrics, logs, and alarms so you can see how your data pipelines behave and get alerted when they fail.

scenes.title: The Pillars of Observability
bullets: Metrics are numeric time series like CPU usage or job duration you can graph and alarm on.
Logs capture detailed text output from your jobs for debugging what went wrong.
Alarms watch metrics and notify you when a threshold is crossed.
scenes.narration: Observability rests on a few complementary signals. Metrics are numeric time series you graph and set thresholds on, like job duration. Logs record the detailed text your jobs emit, which is invaluable when debugging. Alarms tie the two together by alerting you the moment a metric crosses a limit.

scenes.title: From Failure to Alert
scenes.narration: Consider how a failure becomes an actionable alert. A task fails and writes an error to the log group. A metric filter scans those logs and increments an error count. When that count crosses your alarm threshold, a notification fires so someone can respond quickly.

scenes.title: Creating a Metric Alarm
scenes.code:
aws cloudwatch put-metric-alarm \
  --alarm-name pipeline-errors-high \
  --namespace Custom/DataPipeline \
  --metric-name JobErrors \
  --threshold 1 \
  --comparison-operator GreaterThanOrEqualToThreshold \
  --evaluation-periods 1 \
  --alarm-actions arn:aws:sns:us-east-1:123456789012:alerts
scenes.narration: This command wires up proactive alerting for pipeline failures. It watches a custom JobErrors metric and triggers when the count reaches one or more. The alarm-actions field points to an SNS topic, so when the threshold is breached the team is notified immediately rather than discovering the failure hours later.

scenes.text: Instrument pipelines with metrics, logs, and alarms so failures surface immediately — you cannot fix what you cannot see.
scenes.narration: Reliable pipelines depend on visibility. Emit metrics, capture logs, and set alarms so problems announce themselves the moment they occur, because you can only fix what you can actually observe.
